newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to relax pay ceiling to win reform support.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to relax pay ceiling to win reform support.

text.p: The Brazilian government, seeking to reduce opposition in Congress to its civil service reform bill, will relax a proposed limit on pay and perks for deputies and senior judges, a newspaper said Sunday.
Civil service reform is the government's priority after last week's first approval in the Chamber of Deputies of a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique to stand for re-election.

The reform would give state and municipal governments the chance of resolving their chaotic finances by dismissing currenty unfireable workers and is considered a key tool in Brazil's attempts to narrow its public sector deficit.

But a proposed limit of 10,800 reais on monthly pay and benefits for public sector employees ran into stiff opposition in Congress. Many lawmakers make more than that because they claim pensions for previous jobs in the civil service.
Senior judges were also reported to oppose the proposal which would deny them extra income from teaching posts.

"We can't insist that a judge who is also a teacher should work and not be paid for it or that a parliamentarian who was elected should give up his pension," Administration Minister Luis Carlos Bresser Pereira told Jornal do Brasil.
To get round the problem, the bill would allow lawmakers to decide to set a new ceiling for their total pay and benefits and those of supreme court judges, the minister said.

The reform is due to be put to a first of two votes in the Chamber of Deputies in the week beginning February 17, after Carnival, he said. As a constitutional amendment it needs a three-fifths majority in each vote before advancing to the Senate.
